Monday.title: Easy ride
how: Then 45 min steady: you could hold a conversation in full sentences. If you can't, slow down.
Last 5 min very easy, then the 10-min cool-down below.

evidence.text: Most endurance training in successful programs is easy (about 80%), with a small hard dose (Seiler's polarized-training research).
Cardio fitness was one of the strongest predictors of long life in 120,000 treadmill tests (Mandsager et al., JAMA Netw Open, 2018).

lifts.name: Goblet squat
lifts.why: The squat builds the whole lower body: thighs, glutes and the knees that carry you for life.
lifts.setup: Hold one heavy dumbbell or kettlebell upright against your chest, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
steps: Breathe in and brace as if about to be poked in the stomach.
Sit down between your hips, knees following the toes, whole foot on the floor.
Go as low as you can keep your chest up, then stand up smoothly.
lifts.avoid: Heels lifting, knees caving in, rounding the lower back at the bottom.
lifts.progress: When every set reaches the top of the rep range with good form, add the smallest weight step next time. Past about 45 kg the dumbbell gets awkward to hold: switch to a front-loaded barbell squat.
lifts.home: Goblet squat with one dumbbell or kettlebell.
lifts.gym: Barbell back squat in a rack with safeties, or hack squat, 6–8 reps.
lifts.cue: Breathe in and brace as if about to be poked in the stomach.

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.
Roughly 10+ hard sets per muscle per week, spread over 2+ days, builds muscle well (Schoenfeld and colleagues' volume research, used by Jeff Nippard).

lifts.name: Floor press
lifts.why: Your pressing strength for chest, shoulders and triceps. The floor stops the elbows at a shoulder-friendly depth, so no bench is needed.
lifts.setup: Lie on the floor, knees bent, a dumbbell in each hand over your chest.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the floor.
Lower slowly until your upper arms touch the floor, elbows about 45° from your body.
Pause a moment, then press up without bouncing.
lifts.avoid: Flaring the elbows straight out, bouncing the arms off the floor.
lifts.progress: When every set reaches the top of the rep range with good form, add the smallest weight step next time.
lifts.home: Dumbbell floor press, lying on the floor.
lifts.cue: Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the floor.

video.title: How to do the floor press

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.

pic.note: Picture shows a barbell; dumbbells move the same way.

lifts.name: Pull-up
lifts.why: The best upper-back and arm builder there is, and it trains the grip that tracks with a long life.
lifts.setup: Hands on the bar a little wider than your shoulders, palms facing away.
steps: Start from a full hang, shoulders pulled down away from the ears.
Pull your chest toward the bar, elbows driving toward your back pockets.
Lower slowly, about 3 seconds, all the way to a full hang.
lifts.avoid: Kicking or swinging, half reps, dropping fast.
lifts.progress: Fewer than 5? Jump to the top and lower slowly for 5 seconds, 5 reps (no band needed). When you hit 3 × 10, hold a dumbbell between your feet.
lifts.gym: Pull-ups, or neutral-grip lat pulldown for 8–10.
lifts.cue: Start from a full hang, shoulders pulled down away from the ears.

video.title: The best way to do pull-ups for a wide back

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.
Low grip strength predicted earlier death across 17 countries (Leong et al., Lancet, 2015).

lifts.noGear: No bar: one-arm dumbbell row, other hand on the chair seat, 10 per side.

lifts.name: Romanian deadlift
lifts.why: Builds the hamstrings and glutes and teaches the hip hinge that protects your back when you lift anything.
lifts.setup: Stand tall holding the barbell (or two dumbbells) in front of your thighs, feet hip-width.
steps: Soften the knees and push your hips straight back.
Let the weight slide down your thighs, back flat, until the hamstrings stretch (usually just below the knee).
Squeeze the glutes and stand up tall.
lifts.avoid: Rounding the back, bending the knees into a squat, letting the weight drift away from the legs.
lifts.progress: When every set reaches the top of the rep range with good form, add the smallest weight step next time.
lifts.cue: Soften the knees and push your hips straight back.

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.

lifts.name: Bulgarian split squat
lifts.why: One leg at a time: strength, balance and knee health in one move, with no bench needed.
lifts.setup: Stand about two feet in front of the chair, top of your back foot on the seat.
steps: Drop the back knee straight down.
Let the front knee travel forward over the toes as you go lower.
Push through the whole front foot to stand up. Do all reps on one side, then switch.
lifts.avoid: Front heel lifting, wobbling side to side, a chair that slides (put it against a wall).
lifts.progress: Bodyweight until 10 clean reps, then hold dumbbells. When every set reaches the top of the rep range with good form, add the smallest weight step next time.
lifts.home: Back foot on the chair seat, dumbbells when bodyweight gets easy.
lifts.gym: Back foot on a bench, dumbbells.
lifts.cue: Drop the back knee straight down.

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.
Not being able to stand 10 seconds on one leg in mid-life was linked to higher death risk (Araújo et al., BJSM, 2022).

lifts.name: Lateral raise
lifts.why: Side shoulders give the upper body its width, and the big presses barely train them. Light weight, strict form.
lifts.setup: Stand tall, a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides, elbows slightly bent.
steps: Raise the arms out to the sides, leading with the elbows, up to shoulder height.
Pause a moment, then lower slowly, about 2–3 seconds.
Keep the shoulders down, away from the ears.
lifts.avoid: Swinging the body, shrugging, going heavy and using momentum.
lifts.progress: Add reps before weight; the smallest dumbbell step is a big jump here. When every set reaches the top of the rep range with good form, add the smallest weight step next time.
lifts.cue: Raise the arms out to the sides, leading with the elbows, up to shoulder height.

evidence.text: Roughly 10+ hard sets per muscle per week, spread over 2+ days, builds muscle well (Schoenfeld and colleagues' volume research, used by Jeff Nippard).

lifts.name: Ab wheel rollout
lifts.why: Trains the core to stop the lower back from arching: the core's real job when you lift and carry.
lifts.setup: Kneel on a folded towel, hands on the wheel under your shoulders.
steps: Tuck the ribs down and squeeze the glutes.
Roll out slowly only as far as your lower back stays flat.
Pull back with your abs, not your hips.
lifts.avoid: Lower back sagging, hips shooting back first on the return.
lifts.progress: Roll a little farther each week. 3 × 10 to full stretch from the knees is excellent.
lifts.gym: Ab wheel, or cable crunch for 10–12.
lifts.cue: Tuck the ribs down and squeeze the glutes.

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.

lifts.name: Farmer carry
lifts.why: Grip, core, shoulders and posture all at once. Grip strength is one of the best-studied markers of a long life.
lifts.setup: A heavy kettlebell in each hand, handles in the middle of your palms.
steps: Stand tall, shoulders down and back.
Walk with short, quick steps, eyes forward.
Set them down with a flat back.
lifts.avoid: Leaning, shrugging, letting the weights swing.
lifts.progress: Add weight when 40 m feels easy. A strong long-term target: your body weight split between both hands.
lifts.gym: Heavy dumbbells or a trap bar.
lifts.cue: Stand tall, shoulders down and back.

evidence.text: Low grip strength predicted earlier death across 17 countries (Leong et al., Lancet, 2015).

cooldown.goal: Settle the heart rate, use the warm muscles for mobility, and practice the moves that predict a long life.

lifts.name: Deadlift
lifts.why: The biggest whole-body strength lift: back, hips, legs and grip. Done well, it makes everyday lifting safe.
lifts.setup: Bar over the middle of your feet, feet hip-width, hands just outside the legs.
steps: Shins to the bar, hips down until the back is flat, chest up.
Take the slack out of the bar, then push the floor away.
Stand tall, then lower with control, hips back first.
lifts.avoid: Rounding the back, jerking the bar, letting it drift forward.
lifts.progress: Start light and add the smallest step each session while every rep looks the same. When every set reaches the top of the rep range with good form, add the smallest weight step next time.
lifts.cue: Shins to the bar, hips down until the back is flat, chest up.

video.title: Build a bigger deadlift with perfect technique

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.

lifts.name: Overhead press
lifts.why: Builds the shoulders and keeps them strong overhead, a range many people lose with age.
lifts.setup: Sit on the chair, back flat against its upright back, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
steps: Brace, ribs down.
Press straight up until the arms are long, head slightly forward at the top.
Lower slowly to the shoulders.
lifts.avoid: Arching the lower back off the chair, pressing forward instead of up.
lifts.progress: When every set reaches the top of the rep range with good form, add the smallest weight step next time.
lifts.home: Seated dumbbell press, back against the chair.
lifts.gym: Standing dumbbell or barbell overhead press.

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.

clip.note: Demo is standing; you sit with your back on the chair.

lifts.name: Row
lifts.why: Balances all the pressing and sitting: upper back, rear shoulders and posture.
lifts.setup: Bent over with a flat back holding the barbell, or one hand on the chair seat with a dumbbell in the other.
steps: Let the arm(s) hang long.
Pull the elbows toward your hips, squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Pause, then lower slowly.
lifts.avoid: Jerking the torso up, shrugging toward the ears.
lifts.progress: When every set reaches the top of the rep range with good form, add the smallest weight step next time.
lifts.home: Bent-over barbell row, or one-arm dumbbell row with a hand on the chair.

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.
Roughly 10+ hard sets per muscle per week, spread over 2+ days, builds muscle well (Schoenfeld and colleagues' volume research, used by Jeff Nippard).

lifts.name: Knee strength
lifts.why: Strengthens the front of the knee and thigh through a long range, a Knees Over Toes staple for durable knees.
lifts.setup: Kneel on a folded towel, knees hip-width, body straight from knees to head.
steps: Lean back slowly, hips straight, only as far as you can control.
Come back up the same way.
Then 1 set of single-leg glute bridges, 10 per side, for the back of the leg.
lifts.avoid: Bending at the hips, dropping past the range you control.
lifts.progress: Lean a little farther back each week. Add a small weight at your chest when 10 reps are easy.
lifts.home: Reverse Nordic on the floor, then single-leg glute bridges.
lifts.gym: Nordic curl on a Nordic bench, or lying leg curl for 8–12.
lifts.cue: Lean back slowly, hips straight, only as far as you can control.

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.

lifts.limits: Coach-led drill. Long-range knee work is well supported; research on this exact drill is limited.

lifts.name: Calf raise
lifts.why: Strong calves and Achilles carry the ankles and knees through every step, stair and pedal stroke. A Knees Over Toes staple.
lifts.setup: Stand on one foot on a stair edge or the flat floor, fingertips on the wall or the chair back for balance.
steps: Rise as high as you can onto the ball of the foot.
Pause 1 second at the top.
Lower slowly, about 3 seconds, heel all the way down (below the step if you use one).
lifts.avoid: Bouncing, rolling onto the outside of the foot, rushing the way down.
lifts.progress: When 15 slow reps per side are easy, hold a dumbbell in the same-side hand.
lifts.home: One leg at a time, on a stair or the floor.
lifts.gym: Standing or seated calf-raise machine, or the same on a step.
lifts.cue: Rise as high as you can onto the ball of the foot.

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.

lifts.name: Curl and triceps
lifts.why: Direct arm work adds size the big lifts miss, for little time.
lifts.setup: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand.
steps: Curl both dumbbells up, elbows still, lower slowly.
Then one overhead triceps extension: one dumbbell held in both hands behind your head, press up.
That's one round. Rest, repeat.
lifts.avoid: Swinging the body, elbows drifting forward on curls.
lifts.progress: When every set reaches the top of the rep range with good form, add the smallest weight step next time.
lifts.home: Dumbbell curls, then an overhead dumbbell extension.
lifts.gym: Cable or dumbbell curls, then cable overhead extension.
lifts.cue: Curl both dumbbells up, elbows still, lower slowly.

evidence.text: Roughly 10+ hard sets per muscle per week, spread over 2+ days, builds muscle well (Schoenfeld and colleagues' volume research, used by Jeff Nippard).

clip.note: Shows the curl; the triceps press follows.

lifts.name: Hanging knee raise
lifts.why: Lower abs and grip together, plus a free shoulder stretch from the hang.
lifts.setup: Hang from the bar, shoulders active.
steps: Curl your knees up toward your chest, rounding the lower back a little.
Lower slowly, no swinging.
lifts.progress: When 3 × 12 is easy, straighten the legs a little more each week.
lifts.cue: Curl your knees up toward your chest, rounding the lower back a little.

evidence.text: Low grip strength predicted earlier death across 17 countries (Leong et al., Lancet, 2015).

lifts.noGear: No bar: lying leg raises on the floor, lower back pressed down, 10–15 reps.

lifts.name: Side plank
lifts.why: One of the McGill Big 3 for a strong, healthy lower back.
lifts.setup: Lie on your side, elbow under the shoulder, knees bent to start.
steps: Lift the hips so your body is a straight line.
Breathe normally and hold.
lifts.progress: Knees bent, then straight legs, then 45 seconds.
lifts.cue: Lift the hips so your body is a straight line.

evidence.text: ACSM review of resistance training (2026): progressive overload, 2+ days a week, sets near failure build muscle and strength.

lifts.name: Suitcase carry
lifts.why: One heavy weight in one hand trains the side core to keep you upright: carrying groceries, luggage, kids.
lifts.setup: One heavy kettlebell in one hand.
steps: Stand perfectly upright, don't lean away.
Walk with short steps. Switch hands.
lifts.avoid: Leaning toward or away from the weight.
lifts.progress: Add weight when 30 m feels easy.
lifts.cue: Stand perfectly upright, don't lean away.

evidence.text: Low grip strength predicted earlier death across 17 countries (Leong et al., Lancet, 2015).

cooldown.goal: Settle the heart rate, use the warm muscles for mobility, and practice the moves that predict a long life.

items.name: Easy walk outside
items.cue: Step outside if you can: this doubles as your morning light.

items.name: Couch stretch
items.cue: Back knee on a cushion against the couch or wall, squeeze that glute, stay tall.
items.home: Against the couch or a wall.

items.name: 90/90 hip switches
items.cue: Sit with both knees bent at 90°, rotate both knees side to side, stay tall.

items.name: Open book
items.cue: Lie on your side, knees bent, open the top arm across to the other side, follow it with your eyes.

items.name: Dead hang
items.cue: Relaxed hang, breathe. No bar: lat stretch on all fours (sink hips back, arms long).
items.home: Your pull-up bar (no bar: all-fours lat stretch).

items.name: Single-leg stand
items.cue: Stand on one foot, tall. When it's easy, close your eyes.
items.why: Not being able to stand 10 seconds on one leg in mid-life was linked to higher death risk (Araújo et al., BJSM, 2022).

items.name: Floor get-ups
items.cue: Sit down on the floor and stand back up using as little help from your hands as you can.
items.why: The sit-to-rise test (getting up off the floor) tracked with survival (Brito et al., Eur J Prev Cardiol, 2012).

items.name: Physiological sighs
items.cue: Two inhales through the nose (the second one short, to top up), then one long slow exhale through the mouth. Repeat.
items.why: 5 min a day of cyclic sighing improved mood more than mindfulness meditation in a month-long trial (Balban et al., Cell Rep Med, 2023).

longevity.name: Morning light
longevity.dose: 5–10 min outside within an hour of waking
longevity.why: Sets the body clock for better sleep and morning alertness.

longevity.name: No cold shower today
longevity.dose: Wait about 6 hours after lifting
longevity.why: Cold water right after lifting reduced muscle growth over 12 weeks (Roberts et al., J Physiol, 2015). Muscle is goal one, so keep cold to ride days, if you like it.

longevity.name: Protein
longevity.dose: About 1.6 g per kg of body weight a day; a good serving with breakfast
longevity.why: Protein above about 1.6 g per kg of body weight a day adds little more muscle (Morton et al., BJSM, 2018).

longevity.name: Dead-hang target
longevity.dose: Build toward 2 minutes total; test once a month
longevity.why: Low grip strength predicted earlier death across 17 countries (Leong et al., Lancet, 2015). Peter Attia uses a 2-minute hang as a benchmark.

longevity.name: Sleep basics
longevity.dose: Same wake time every day, dark and cool room, last caffeine 8–10 hours before bed
longevity.why: Sleep is when muscle repairs; Huberman and Attia rank it with exercise.

mental.name: Priory · Body Scan
mental.dose: 3–5 min, after the workout or any time today

Friday.title: 4×4 build-up (4×3 min)
Friday.summary: 4 rounds of 3 min hard, 3 min easy.
how: 10 min warm-up, building from easy to moderate.
4 rounds: 3 min hard at 8–9 out of 10 (only a few words at a time), then 3 min easy spinning.
Then the 10-min cool-down below; keep the easy spin a little longer after hard rounds.
The hard rounds grow from 2 to 3 to 4 minutes over the first weeks, so you earn the full 4×4 by week 7.
Friday.why: Once a week, this is the best-studied way to raise heart fitness (VO2 max), one of the strongest markers of long life.

evidence.text: 4×4 intervals raised VO2 max more than steady riding at the same total work (Helgerud et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc, 2007).
Cardio fitness was one of the strongest predictors of long life in 120,000 treadmill tests (Mandsager et al., JAMA Netw Open, 2018).

Friday.safety: Pick a quiet stretch of road with no stop lights for the hard rounds. Lights on in the dark.
prep: Front and rear lights on (dark until about 6:40).
Water bottle; add electrolytes if it's hot and humid.
Squeeze the tires and test the brakes.

effort.feel: 3–4 out of 10. You can talk in full sentences; you could breathe through your nose.

effort.use: Only the end of the 4×4 warm-up.

effort.feel: 8–9 out of 10. A few words at a time, legs burning by the end of each round.

cooldown.goal: Let the heart rate come down slowly, then loosen what the bike tightens.

longevity.name: Steps and a walk after meals

longevity.why: Health benefits of daily steps level off around 7,000–8,000 (Paluch et al., Lancet Public Health, 2022). A short walk after eating also blunts the blood-sugar spike, which matters on a desk day.

Saturday.title: Rest or mobility
Saturday.summary: Optional 15 min mobility and a walk in the morning light. Rest is fine too.

mobility.name: Cat-cow
mobility.cue: On all fours, round the back up, then let it sink, moving one segment at a time.

mobility.name: 90/90 hip switches
mobility.cue: Both knees at 90°, rotate side to side, stay tall.

mobility.name: Deep squat rocks
mobility.cue: Sink into a deep squat, holding the chair if needed, rock gently side to side.

mobility.name: Open book
mobility.cue: Side-lying, open the top arm across, follow it with your eyes.

mobility.name: Figure-four hip stretch
mobility.cue: On your back, ankle over the other knee, pull gently.

mobility.name: Dead hang
mobility.cue: Relaxed hang (no bar: heavy kettlebell hold).
mobility.why: Low grip strength predicted earlier death across 17 countries (Leong et al., Lancet, 2015).

mobility.name: McGill Big 3
mobility.cue: Curl-up, bird dog, side plank: 8–10 sec holds, a few reps each.

mobility.name: Single-leg stand and floor get-ups
mobility.cue: Balance on each foot, then sit down and stand up with as little hand help as you can.
mobility.why: Not being able to stand 10 seconds on one leg in mid-life was linked to higher death risk (Araújo et al., BJSM, 2022).

Saturday.why: Moving every joint through its full range keeps it that way. Balance and getting up off the floor are two of the simplest predictors of a long, independent life.

evidence.text: Not being able to stand 10 seconds on one leg in mid-life was linked to higher death risk (Araújo et al., BJSM, 2022).
The sit-to-rise test (getting up off the floor) tracked with survival (Brito et al., Eur J Prev Cardiol, 2012).

Saturday.source: JR Stretch · CaliMove · Movement by David · McGill · Huberman

optional.note: Only if you feel fresh. A third lifting day builds muscle faster.

swap.title: Bad-weather swap: kettlebell circuit
how: 5 rounds, 1 min rest between rounds (about 25 min):
swap.note: Keep it moderate, about 6–7 out of 10, so you're fresh for the lifting days.

rules: Missed a lifting day? Do it the next day and push the rest of the week along. Never two lifting days back to back, never two workouts in one day.
Rain or lightning at ride time: do the kettlebell circuit instead.
This week's riding: about 149 min. Guidelines ask for at least 150 min of moderate activity a week; walks add to it.
